<!--redteam:v1 {"owner":"AI-DOOM-b743906b-281a-4ba5-939c-d5913cc9d39b","findings":["RT-20261106-cf07f8"],"patterns":["docstring-mismatch"],"severity":"NIT"}-->

## What was wrong
The docstring of `Polynomial.Monic.tschirnhausRootMap_surjective` said every root of the Tschirnhaus transform of a monic polynomial is the image of a root of the original, but the statement also assumes `hs : (f.map (algebraMap K L)).Splits`, which the docstring omitted. Without it the claim fails: for `K = L = ℚ`, `f = X^2 - 2`, `T = X^2` the transform is `(Y - 2)^2` with root `2`, while `f` has no root in `ℚ`. Raised by Haiku survey h201-haiku; verified from the source.

## Evidence
`sed -n 299,310p TauCeti/RingTheory/Polynomial/Tschirnhaus.lean` on origin/main shows a docstring without the splitting condition above a statement with `hs`; the neighbouring `rootSet_tschirnhausPolynomial` and the field version `tschirnhausRootMap_surjective` state it.

## The fix
Docstring only: it now says that if the monic `f` splits in the domain `L`, every root in `L` of its transform is the image of a root of `f` in `L`. No code changed. `TauCeti.RingTheory.Polynomial.Tschirnhaus` builds clean; `scripts/lint-style.sh` clean. No open PR touches the file.

The second Haiku lead for this file (the monic CommRing lemmas as duplicates of the field lemmas) was checked and refuted: the monic versions hold over any commutative ring and do not follow from the field versions, which in turn drop monicity.

entry.content:
feat: complete weak Whitney map spaces on open domains (#29593)

This PR proves completeness of the existing weak Whitney topology on native maps from an arbitrary open subset of a normed space, supplying the open coefficient-map spaces needed for smooth bundle sections.

Roadmap: ComplexKahlerGeometry

Partially implements the smooth-section Fréchet prerequisites in [K5a, real and complex-coefficient analysis on real manifolds](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ComplexKahlerGeometry/README.md#L718-L724). This is also a transitive prerequisite for the section-space inputs to PseudoholomorphicCurveAnalysis #1793.

The open-set Taylor-series limit theorem uses locally uniform convergence of the actual coefficients and Mathlib's derivative-limit theorem on open sets. The existing whole-source theorem now specializes this result to the universal set. No completeness of the target is required when the coefficient limits are already given.

`ContMDiffMap.openWeakWhitneyJet` records the derivatives of the existing native map carrier on the open source. Its comparison with every inherited chart jet proves that it induces precisely the existing manifold weak Whitney topology. The compatible derivative uniformity is selected by the existing `TauCeti.ManifoldWeakWhitney` scope. The jet image is closed, giving completeness for complete targets at every finite and smooth exponent. Analytic regularity is excluded. With explicit sigma-compactness of the open source, the uniformity is countably generated and the topology is metrizable. No finite-dimensionality or separability of the target is assumed.

The empty-source case does not choose a point. Real bases with complex targets use the actual real normed-space structure on the target. Global section reconstruction, cover/frame independence, continuous bundle restriction and Montel results remain subsequent K5a work; this PR supplies their local completion input without introducing a section carrier or topology.

The canonical open-chart target identification and homeomorphism are public in the core `ExtChartAt` module under `TopologicalSpace.Opens`.

The elementary arbitrary-extension smoothness theorem is public in `ContMDiffMap/Extension`, available without the Whitney layer.

Original proper-open/real-base-complex-target, empty/order/countability consumers and the core-chart consumer pass; a new Extension-only consumer checks the arbitrary-field extension theorem without importing Whitney theory. Style, staged dot notation (zero new), and diff checks pass.

This PR identifies the pointwise cokernel of `SLₙ(R) → PGLₙ(R)` with `Rˣ / (Rˣ)ⁿ`. Construct the determinant-class homomorphism, prove its kernel is exactly the SL image, prove surjectivity for nonempty matrix indices, and give the induced multiplicative equivalence with its representative value law. For the normalized rank-one adjoint torus, prove that `[diag(a,1)]` lifts precisely when `a` is a square unit; in particular `[diag(2,1)]` over ℚ does not lift.

Advance `ChevalleyGroups/README.md`, milestone C6, “Chevalley's comparison theorem”, item “Extension by the actual torus”, which explicitly requires the distinction that `G_sc(A₁) → PGL₂` over ℚ has cokernel `ℚˣ / ℚˣ²`. entry.title: feat: open contact loci and uniform affine deformations (#28976)
entry.content:
feat: open contact loci and uniform affine deformations (#28976)

This PR proves that contactness is open for continuous covector/bilinear-form families on a finite-dimensional space, and that two such pairs agreeing on a subset have a contact affine interpolation on an open neighborhood, uniformly over any compact parameter set. Keep this as the complete coefficient-level prerequisite for contact deformation arguments; no manifold neighborhood or isotopy theorem is claimed.

Advance `SymplecticGeometry/ContactGeometry/README.md`, milestone CG3, “Darboux and Gray stability”: the contact Darboux proof must keep its local contact-Moser path contact while shrinking the spatial neighborhood over the compact time interval. The linear normal form and horizontal contact-Moser equation already exist on main. The explicit downstream consumer is CG5, “Isotropic and Legendrian neighborhoods”, which requires that forms agreeing in full value and exterior derivative along the zero section have contact affine interpolation on a neighborhood for every t ∈ [0,1]. In a local tangent-bundle trivialization, apply `exists_isOpen_isContact_affine` to the covector values and exterior-derivative bilinear forms, with K = [0,1]. After this PR, the manifold/trivialization adapter and integration of the resulting time-dependent contact-Moser field remain before the contact Darboux/Gray and Legendrian neighborhood theorems can be concluded.

Roadmap: SymplecticGeometry

<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"SymplecticGeometry","id":"contact-affine-homotopy-neighborhood"}-->

Add `TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Module/Contact.lean` (98 lines), with two public theorems and no new definitions. The first theorem uses the existing `Module.Dual.isContact_iff_nondegenerate_symplectizationForm` and Mathlib's determinant criterion for nondegeneracy. The second uses Mathlib's `IsCompact.eventually_forall_of_forall_eventually`; compactness is needed only for the parameter set, not the agreement locus. No topology or norm on the vector space, alternation assumption on the bilinear forms, or closedness of the agreement locus is imposed. The field needs continuous ring operations and closed singletons, not continuity of inversion.

References credited in the module: Geiges, *An Introduction to Contact Topology*, §2.5, and Kriegl–Michor, *The Convenient Setting of Global Analysis*, Proposition 43.18. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored.

entry.title: feat: coordinate quantiles of count-vector laws (#25761)
entry.content:
feat: coordinate quantiles of count-vector laws (#25761)

This PR adds the coordinate quantiles of the count-vector laws required by the non-scalar coverage list of Layer 13 (`StandardDistributions/README.md`, "Layer 13: quantile formulas and coverage of all families"), whose first bullet asks for "Multinomial, Dirichlet-multinomial, and multivariate hypergeometric: coordinate Binomial/Beta-binomial/hypergeometric quantiles" and "Negative multinomial: coordinate and total negative-binomial quantiles".

Roadmap: StandardDistributions

<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"StandardDistributions","id":"count-vector-coordinate-quantiles"}-->

Each new file transfers the existing scalar quantile API through the existing marginal identification and states the result in the vector law's own parameters. Following the roadmap's instruction to prove explicit crossings rather than restate `sInf`, each quantile is characterized as the least count at which the explicit cumulative mass reaches the level, and each file gives both one-sided endpoint limits.

- `Multinomial/Quantile.lean`: cell `i` is `Bin(n, p i)` (via `map_eval_multinomialMeasure`). The crossing is the regularized incomplete Beta function at `1 - p i`. The lower limit is `n` for a cell of weight one and `0` otherwise, and the upper limit is `0` for a cell of weight zero and `n` otherwise.
- `DirichletMultinomial/Quantile.lean`: with at least two categories, coordinate `i` is beta-binomial with shapes `a i` and `∑ j ≠ i, a j` (via `map_eval_dirichletMultinomialMeasure`), with the finite beta-binomial cumulative sum as crossing and limits `0` and `n`.
- `MultivariateHypergeometric/Quantile.lean`: for `n ≤ ∑ j, K j`, coordinate `i` is hypergeometric with population `∑ j, K j` and `K i` marked (via `map_eval_multivariateHypergeometricMeasure`), with limits `n - (∑ j, K j - K i)` and `min (K i) n`.
- `NegativeMultinomial/Quantile.lean`: coordinate `i` is negative binomial with success probability `p₀ / (p₀ + p i)` and the total is negative binomial with success probability `p₀` (via `map_eval_negativeMultinomialMeasure` and `map_sum_negativeMultinomialMeasure`). For positive shape the crossings are incomplete-Beta. The upper limits are `⊤` except at the Dirac boundaries, which are `r = 0 ∨ p i = 0` for a coordinate and `r = 0 ∨ p₀ = 1` for the total.

`Multinomial/Marginal.lean` also gains the `@[simp]` lemmas `multinomialCellProbability_eq_zero_iff` and `multinomialCellProbability_eq_one_iff`, which state the multinomial endpoint limits in terms of the simplex weights.

After this PR the count-vector items of Layer 13's non-scalar coverage are done. The Dirichlet Beta-coordinate quantiles and the finite uniform/categorical label quantiles remain open on that list.

Reference: N. L. Johnson, S. Kotz, N. Balakrishnan, *Discrete Multivariate Distributions*, Wiley, 1997, Chapters 35, 36 and 39. No Mathlib material is vendored.

entry.title: refactor(KnotTheory/Grid): build the six matrix-coefficient maps on G…
entry.content:
refactor(KnotTheory/Grid): build the six matrix-coefficient maps on GC⁻ from one constructor (#28626)

Roadmap: CombinatorialHeegaardFloer
<!--redteam:v1 {"owner":"AI-DOOM-b743906b-281a-4ba5-939c-d5913cc9d39b","findings":["RT-20261105-6c5390"],"patterns":["duplicated-construction-across-siblings"],"severity":"MINOR"}-->

## What was wrong
Six endomorphisms of `GC⁻` were each built by hand as "the linear map with these matrix coefficients", with the same term `Finsupp.linearCombination (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) fun x => Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun y => M x y` and the same pair of lemmas (`_single_apply`, `_apply_apply`) proved six times over: `GridDiagram.hexagonMap` and `GridDiagram.initialHexagonMap` (`Commutation/Hexagon.lean`), `GridDiagram.crossingChangeHomotopy` (`CrossingChange/Hexagon.lean`), `GridDiagram.XHomotopy` (`XHomotopy/Basic.lean`), `GridDiagram.filteredDifferential` (`Filtered/Basic.lean`) and `GridDiagram.signedUnblockedDifferential` (`SignAssignment/Differential.lean`). The library had no name for the construction, although it already names its semilinear twin `GridChain.renameMatrixMap`.

## Evidence
The red-team probe (a `module` file importing `TauCeti.KnotTheory.Grid.Commutation.Hexagon`, `lake env lean` at e8758b7b2f: no messages) defines the constructor with its two lemmas and shows each of `hexagonMap`, `initialHexagonMap` and `commutationHomotopy` equal to it at the corresponding coefficient function by `ext x y; simp` (resp. `simp only` with the `_single_apply` lemmas). The finding record RT-20261105-6c5390 carries the probe verbatim. Astra review is pending (Astra is unavailable until 2026-11-09; this change is queued in the red team's pending-Astra list).

## The fix
- `Unblocked.lean`: new `GridChain.matrixMap (M : GridState n → GridState n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)`, placed next to `renameMatrixMap` (its semilinear version), with `matrixMap_single_apply` (`matrixMap R M (single x p) y = p * M x y`) and `matrixMap_apply_apply` (`matrixMap R M c y = c.sum fun x p => p * M x y`).
- The six maps are now `GridChain.matrixMap R <coefficient function>`; their statements, names and `@[simp]` attributes are unchanged, and each `_single_apply` / `_apply_apply` is a one-line instance of the two constructor lemmas. `XHomotopy_single` (the whole-row form) now follows from `XHomotopy_single_apply` by `Finsupp.ext`, so the two lemmas swap places.
- No declaration is deleted or renamed. `unblockedDifferential` is left as it is: it goes through `unblockedDifferentialOnGenerator`, which has its own API, and converting it is a separate topic.

## Why the changed definition is still the standard one
The standard definition (Manolescu, Ozsváth, Szabó and Thurston, *On combinatorial link Floer homology*, Sections 2 and 3.1; Ozsváth, Stipsicz and Szabó, *Grid Homology for Knots and Links*, Chapter 4 and Section 5.1) gives every one of these maps by its matrix coefficients: the generator `x` goes to `∑_y M(x, y) · y` for a coefficient `M(x, y)` in `𝔽[V_0, …, V_{n-1}]` that counts rectangles or hexagons with their `O`-weights. The Tau Ceti maps are each exactly that linear extension; `GridChain.matrixMap M` is the same `Finsupp.linearCombination` term, so each map is definitionally unchanged (the old body was `matrixMap`'s body with `fun y => M x y` in place of `M x`, an eta-expansion). Every downstream statement keeps its meaning, since nothing but the spelling of the body changed; the whole-library build of every module mentioning one of the six maps passes with the old proofs. Checked: (a) each docstring (they describe the coefficient formula, which is still what the body says), (b) the roadmap (CombinatorialHeegaardFloer README, item 5: commutation invariance through pentagon maps and hexagon homotopies), (c) the references above, (d) the review-site standard reviews of `hexagonMap` and `hexagonWeight` (both state the map as `x ↦ ∑_y c_{xy} y`, no noes).

Overlapping open PRs: #28549 and #28590 also touch `Commutation/Hexagon.lean` (in earlier regions; `git merge-tree` against both heads is clean), and the long-standing #26591 lists `SignAssignment/Differential.lean` (its conflicts are with `origin/main` already and not in that file).

Built: `TauCeti.KnotTheory.Grid.Unblocked`, the five other changed modules and every module mentioning one of the six maps (27 targets, 211 modules replayed or built), zero errors and warnings; `scripts/lint-style.sh` clean; Batteries `unusedArguments` lint over the six changed modules clean.

entry.title: feat: the fibre criterion for relative effective Cartier divisors aft…
entry.content:
feat: the fibre criterion for relative effective Cartier divisors after base change (#28759)

This PR proves the fibre criterion for relative effective Cartier divisors over an arbitrary base, for families that are base changes of a locally noetherian flat family. This is the form the criterion takes after a family has been spread out to a noetherian base. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat with `X` locally noetherian, let `I` be an ideal sheaf on `X` whose closed subscheme is flat over `S`, and let `g : T ⟶ S` be any morphism. Then the pullback of `I` to `X ×_S T` is a relative effective Cartier divisor over `T` if and only if its fibre over every point of `T` (`isRelativeEffectiveCartier_comap_fst_iff_forall_isEffectiveCartier_comap_fiberι`), or over every geometric point of `T` (`…_comap_fst_of_isAlgClosed`), is an effective Cartier divisor. Neither `T` nor `X ×_S T` needs to be locally noetherian. The sufficiency direction only asks about the fibres of `I` over points in the image of `g` (`isRelativeEffectiveCartier_comap_fst_of_isEffectiveCartier_comap_fiberι`).

Roadmap target: `ModularCurves/README.md`, Layer 0, §0A *Relative effective Cartier divisors*, item 1: "Prove the limit/descent version used after spreading out to an arbitrary base." Earlier partial PRs proved the rest of item 1 with `X` locally noetherian: #21321 the local algebra, #23473 the stalk criterion, #23763 residue-field fibres, #27087 geometric fibres. Items 2–7 were already on main. This PR does the descent step. A fibre of the base change over `t` is the base change of the fibre of `I` over `g t` along the field extension `κ(g t) → κ(t)`, so it descends. The noetherian criterion then gives a local nonzerodivisor equation of `I` near the image in `X` of each point of `X ×_S T`, and that equation stays a nonzerodivisor after base change because the quotient is flat.

What remains of the milestone after this PR is the spreading out itself, which covers a family over `T` that is only known to be of finite presentation. One must produce a noetherian model `X₀ ⟶ S₀` and an ideal sheaf `I₀` such that `X₀` and the closed subscheme of `I₀` are flat over `S₀`. That needs flatness to descend to a finite stage of a limit (EGA IV 11.2.6, Stacks 05LY), which the 0E spreading-out material has to provide. It is not on main.

To support this, the PR makes the existing noetherian criteria pointwise. The old global theorems become one-line corollaries; their statements do not change:
- `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EffectiveCartierDivisor/Stalk.lean`: `exists_eq_span_singleton_of_map_germ_eq_span_singleton`. On a locally noetherian scheme, a nonzerodivisor equation of the stalk at `x` spreads to an affine open neighbourhood of `x`. Its proof is the body of the old `isEffectiveCartier_of_exists_map_germ_eq_span_singleton`, which now just calls it.
- `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EffectiveCartierDivisor/Fiber.lean`: `exists_eq_span_singleton_of_isEffectiveCartier_comap_fiberι`. If the fibre over `f x` is effective Cartier, `I` has a nonzerodivisor equation near `x`. The old `isEffectiveCartier_of_isEffectiveCartier_comap_fiberι` is now its corollary. The proof also has to check that the field-valued point `Spec κ(p) ⟶ Spec A ⟶ S` lies over `f x`.
- The private `isEffectiveCartier_comap_fst_SpecMap_comp_fromSpecResidueField_iff` becomes the public `isEffectiveCartier_comap_fst_comp_iff`, for an arbitrary `h ≫ g`: base change along `h ≫ g` versus base change along `g` and then along `h`. The two existing field-point lemmas now use it, and so does the new geometric criterion.

The main theorem is local on `X ×_S T`. Near a point `z`, take an affine open `U ⊆ X` around the image of `z` on which `I` has a nonzerodivisor equation. The restriction of `I` to `U` is a relative effective Cartier divisor. Its base change to `U ×_S T`, an open subscheme of `X ×_S T` containing `z`, is one by the existing `IsRelativeEffectiveCartier.comap`. The existing locality lemma `isEffectiveCartier_of_forall_exists_isOpenImmersion` glues these. The diff is 2 files, about +190/−55 lines. It adds no definitions or instances.

References, cited in the files: the Stacks Project, *Divisors*, section *Relative effective Cartier divisors*; Katz–Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, §1.2. No Mathlib PR material is vendored.

I checked locally that `lake build`, `lake exe axioms` and `lake exe module-system` pass. `scripts/lint-env.sh` cannot run in this sandbox because `uvx` is not installed. `lake exe runLinter` passes on both changed modules.
